mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS drop > 5% MoM does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over 3 consecutive months signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over 3 consecutive months signals a strengthening demand side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a decrease in GDP (GDPC1) signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decrease does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness during tightening cycles.
